regions.text: the tragedy of the shuttle Challenger.
regions.explanation: From 15.98s to 18.73s (“the tragedy of the shuttle Challenger.”), articulation rate slowed to 4.00 syll/s against 6.29 syll/s in the reference (-36%); that is 1.5× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Stretched words without matching emphasis read as hesitation and dilute the rhythm of the phrase; the audience's attention drifts between content words. Fix: Tighten these words to the reference pace; keep length only on the stressed word.

regions.explanation: At 40.06s, “perhaps we've forgotten” (3 word(s)) is said twice in a row (recognised here: “this and perhaps we've forgotten ferhaps we've forgotten the courage it took”), adding 740 ms. Going back to repeat words already said signals a lost place or a self-correction; it breaks the flow of the phrase and costs time without adding meaning. Fix: If you stumble, carry on from where you are; rehearse this phrase until it runs in one go.
